root_causes.root_cause: RFC-028 D5 fixed OCR language detection in _recover_picture_results (converters.py) by unioning detect_ocr_langs(filename) with detect_ocr_langs(md), adding 'ara' to Tesseract langs for Arabic-named PDFs. Combined with the existing Fix-3 force_full_page_ocr retry path (client.py ~line 991), the OCR retry now produces 54k chars of Arabic-looking OCR output (up from 1.8k in Run 11) for the scanned 42-page warid-597 document. This OCR output dilutes the repeating numeric-junk text layer ('1651001429') below all _is_garbled_blob thresholds: digit-ratio drops from ~100% to <1% (420 digit chars in 54k total), token-repetition drops far below 30%. validate_tree passes (111 nodes, depth>=2, no garble detected), classify_verdict returns PASS. In Run 11, the OCR retry produced only 1.8k chars (OCR'd with 'eng' model on Arabic pages), validate_tree failed with garbling, doc fell to flat path which stored MARGINAL garbling(ratio=1.00). The regression is that improved OCR language detection paradoxically removed the garble-gate safety net by producing more (but still low-quality) OCR content.
root_causes.code_path: client.py::index() Fix-3 retry (line ~991) -> converters.py::_recover_picture_results D5 lang union (line ~2117) -> helpers.py::_is_garbled_blob digit-ratio check (line 897-901) -> helpers.py::_tree_is_garbled (line 1052-1058) -> helpers.py::validate_tree (line 1142) returns True -> helpers.py::classify_verdict (line 1344) garbled=False -> PASS
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a chars-per-page density floor to validate_tree or classify_verdict for scanned PDFs. warid-597 has 54k chars / 42 pages = ~1303 chars/page, well below the 2000-4000 chars/page expected for government documents. A density check (e.g., if page_count available and chars_per_page < MIN_SCANNED_DENSITY_FLOOR, flag as suspect) would catch this. Alternatively, add an Arabic content validation heuristic: if the filename is Arabic but the OCR output's Arabic-char ratio is low (numeric junk + OCR noise), flag as garbled. A third option is to compare pre-retry and post-retry garble signals in the D4 keep-best logic -- if the pre-retry was garbled and the post-retry has similar garble patterns (same repeating tokens), don't let char-count growth alone override the garble detection.
